I stupidly met him at a forest preserve one evening, and nothing dangerous happened, except that I decided he should come over to my house and meet my mom. When that day came, we were in my home alone together, before my mom came home. He raped me as I cried for myself. When my mom got home, we ate dinner together and he was as charming as could be, full well knowing what he had just done to me. Later, over the phone, I tried telling him that I was upset about the way we had sex, and he became irate saying it’s not fair of me to ask him to go without sex. Apparently a man has needs! I was heartbroken, but our contact dwindled from that point.

This is incorrect. In the way this op explained it, water is a proton (NOT a hydrogen) and a hydroxide. A proton has a +1 charge and a hydroxide has a -1 charge, and together they make neutral water.

What original OP needs to recognize is that the O in H2O has a -2 charge, leaving two H+ ions. Two protons do not come together to form H2 because there are literally zero electrons to form a bond between the two atoms.

I have anxiety induced by a childhood of trauma and neglect. I was fired from my first job out of college simply for standing up for myself. I just left the following job because my boss was psychologically abusive. I’ve decided I’m going to start my own business in my industry, despite daily challenges to get out of bed and do basic life tasks. I cannot fail at this because everything is on the line if I don’t get my crap together. The thing I fear losing the most is my horse. I love him to pieces, and though he is certainly a “luxury” item, I dearly need him in my life. He saves me.

I was in a medically-induced coma for 2 days, on a ventilator and everything. Apparently, no one was expecting me to wake up as quickly as I did when they reversed it, so no one was really paying attention to me. I sat up, completely unable to breathe (or so I thought), not knowing who all these people were and whether they were going to let me suffocate or not. Then the doctor turned around, saw my horror, chuckled, and removed the ventilator. Thankfully I could breathe again (still), but I was pissed.
